cbe156dffb.why: Fact-check error fixed: the card now says that electrons do not feel the strong force at all (leptons carry no colour charge), not that its range keeps it off them. Judge tell fixed: 'side by side' and 'close quarters' are out of the stem, and the key 'right next to it' no longer matches a stem word. The strong force reaches only nearest neighbours (about 2.5 fm, saturation); 2.5 fm is 2.5 trillionths of a mm; 'about 100 times' the proton-proton electric push is confirmed. All three lures are truly wrong. T4 inside-the-atom keys the nucleus's parts, not the force, so this is no re-ask.

06b6b0598d.why: 'Some thirty years' fits a partnership from late 1907 to July 1938. The card's held-back line no longer adds 'as chemists'. Key and lures unchanged and sound: barium (56) is little more than half of uranium (92), the transuranium reading was Fermi's and Berlin's, and the barium appeared only after bombardment. Hahn's letter, Meitner's flight in summer 1938, Christmas in Sweden with Frisch, the word fission, and Hahn's 1944 prize alone are all confirmed. Distinct from af2403a085 (Frisch's test).

7c6e1c0235.why: Safety lane fixed: the chain is set in a reactor's fuel, one split setting off the next, not in a lump of uranium-235. No enrichment, critical-mass or weapon detail anywhere. Key true (2-3 neutrons per split, about 2.43 on average); the lures (heat, the flying fragments, radiation weakening the next) are truly wrong, and the stem's flying pieces make one of them live. Pellet against a ton of coal, and millions of times chemical energy, confirmed. Distinct from eff142c470.

eff142c470.why: Fact-check error fixed: the card says the water carries the heat away 'to make the steam', true of both PWRs (more than 65% of US reactors, where a separate loop boils) and BWRs (energy.gov). Key true (rods absorb neutrons). Slowing is the moderator's job, cooling is the coolant's, bouncing back is a reflector's: all truly wrong. The stem's 'heats water into steam' is loose for a PWR but true at one remove. The turbine and generator are only a premise, so this is no re-ask of T1 energy-changes-form.

994f30454a.why: Fact-check error fixed: the card now says the 2.05 MJ of laser light was fired into the gold can (hohlraum) that held the pellet. Physics Today: the light 'reached the small cylindrical chamber known as a hohlraum', whose X-rays crushed the capsule. Key true by LLNL's definition (scientific breakeven). The grid draw (about 300 MJ), the 3.15 MJ yield, 192 beams, 5 December 2022 and the later shots of more than 8 MJ (8.6 MJ, April 2025) are all confirmed. 'No machine yet makes more electricity than it uses' still holds in November 2026: Realta's June 2026 demo is stated not to be net electricity. The stem's 'aimed at a pellet' is acceptable shorthand.

928d5d3fa3.why: All three fixes are in. The card says 'without any radioactive material escaping', matching DOE's 'without any radiological releases' over more than 2,500 shipments. The lure now reads 'escapes from its casks', which is wrong on that record. The stance fix is in: the card states flatly that the US has no permanent store and Yucca Mountain has been halted since 2010, and that Finland has built Onkalo (licensed 22 October 2026, disposal not yet begun, so 'has built' is right). Key true. Solid fuel, about 2,000 t a year in the US, and the football field are confirmed. Minor: the cask lure is about moving rather than storing, so it is the weakest of the three, but it is still a real fear and plainly wrong. Benefits stated as facts, no verdict.
